prompt: Match each table to how `nightly.sh` loads it.
hint: Three tables, three loads.

pairs.right: Type 2: close the old version, open a new one
Delete the day, insert it again

prompt: Why does `nightly.sh` load `dim_customer` before `fact_sales`?
hint: What does the fact load look up?

choices.text: Alphabetical order
choices.why: The order is a dependency, not a spelling.

choices.text: Facts look up the customer's version
choices.why: Right. A sale needs the version that was current when it happened.

choices.text: `dim_customer` is smaller and finishes faster, which frees memory for the facts
choices.why: Size has nothing to do with it; the facts depend on the dimension.

choices.text: PostgreSQL loads dimensions first by default
choices.why: PostgreSQL knows nothing about dimensions; the script decides.

prompt: After 2 March was appended twice to `marts.sales_log`, it held 830 rows. How many distinct order lines did they describe?
hint: Each line twice.

prompt: When is a plain append safe?
hint: Two conditions, and only one holds up.

choices.text: When the target tells a repeat from a new row
choices.why: Right. A key and a load that refuses or ignores what it already has.

choices.text: When the table is small
choices.why: A small table doubles as easily as a large one.

choices.text: When the pipeline runs at night
choices.why: Night runs are retried like any other.

choices.text: When the source has an `updated_at` column
choices.why: A watermark helps choose rows, but cannot stop a rerun repeating them.

prompt: Why do the `DELETE` and the `INSERT` in `fact_sales.sql` sit inside one transaction?
hint: What would a reader see between them otherwise?

choices.text: PostgreSQL forbids a `DELETE` outside a transaction
choices.why: Every statement runs in some transaction; the point is grouping two.

choices.text: So readers never see the day missing
choices.why: Right. Old rows until the commit, new rows after.

choices.text: To make the insert faster
choices.why: Speed is not the reason.

choices.text: To lock the shop's tables during the load
choices.why: The transaction is in the warehouse; the shop is untouched.

prompt: A refund on 9 March cancels an order from 2 March. With `fact_sales.sql`, how does that reach the fact table?
hint: The load rebuilds a period from staging.

choices.text: The 9 March load updates the old fact row
choices.why: The load deletes and inserts only the day it is given.

choices.text: It never does: facts are written once
choices.why: They can be rebuilt; that is what replacing a period allows.

choices.text: Rerunning the load for 2 March rebuilds the day without the order
choices.why: Right. The day is rebuilt from what the shop says now.

choices.text: A trigger in the warehouse deletes the fact when the order changes
choices.why: There is no such trigger; the warehouse learns by reloading.

prompt: In `fact_sales.sql`, `:'day'` is replaced by a value given to psql on the command line with the option ___.
hint: A single letter after a hyphen, or its long form.

prompt: What does the `WHERE ... IS DISTINCT FROM` on the update in `dim_book.sql` prevent?
hint: What would happen to the 1,199 unchanged books?

choices.text: Inserting a duplicate book
choices.why: `ON CONFLICT` already prevents that.

choices.text: Rewriting unchanged books every night
choices.why: Right. Only the changed rows are written.

choices.text: Updating a book whose price went down
choices.why: A lower price is distinct, so it is updated.

choices.text: A conflict on the ISBN when two books share one
choices.why: The conflict target is `book_id`; ISBNs are unique in the shop.

prompt: A report needs the list price each book had on the day it sold. Why should it not read `dim_book`?
hint: Type 1 keeps only the present.

choices.text: It holds only today's price
choices.why: Right. Old prices are overwritten; the price paid is on the order line.

choices.text: It is updated only once a month
choices.why: It is loaded every night.

choices.text: It holds prices in a different currency from the facts
choices.why: Everything is in cents of reais.

choices.text: It has no `book_id` to join on
choices.why: `book_id` is its primary key.

prompt: A colleague writes `ON CONFLICT (isbn)` against a table with no unique index on `isbn`. What happens?
hint: What does "the existing row" mean without one?

choices.text: Every row is inserted, duplicates included
choices.why: PostgreSQL does not guess; it refuses.

choices.text: PostgreSQL creates the index
choices.why: Nothing is created for you.

choices.text: The statement fails with an error
choices.why: Right. The conflict target must be a unique constraint or index.

choices.text: It falls back to the primary key
choices.why: It does not fall back; it errors.

prompt: Why does `dim_customer.sql` compare with `IS DISTINCT FROM` rather than `<>`?
hint: What is `NULL <> 'SP'`?

choices.text: `<>` does not work on tuples
choices.why: It does; the problem is `NULL`.

choices.text: `IS DISTINCT FROM` is faster
choices.why: Speed is not the reason.

choices.text: A change from `NULL` still counts
choices.why: Right. `<>` with a `NULL` gives `NULL`, and the change is skipped.

choices.text: It ignores case differences in city names
choices.why: It compares exactly.

prompt: After fifteen nights `dim_customer` held 5,413 versions of 5,366 customers. How many versions were closed?
hint: One current version per customer.

prompt: A customer moves to Curitiba at 10:00 and to Londrina at 16:00 on the same day. What does the nightly type 2 load record?
hint: It reads the shop once a night.

choices.text: Two new versions, Curitiba and Londrina
choices.why: Only CDC sees both changes.

choices.text: One new version, Londrina
choices.why: Right. Curitiba was never seen by the nightly read.

choices.text: No change until the next night
choices.why: That night's read sees Londrina.

choices.text: An error, because two changes have the same date
choices.why: Only one change is ever seen.

prompt: Why does the fact load join on `valid_from` and `valid_to` instead of `is_current`?
hint: Think of reloading an old day.

choices.text: So a reload finds the version true at the sale
choices.why: Right. `is_current` would attach old sales to today's city.

choices.text: `is_current` is not indexed
choices.why: Indexing is not the reason.

choices.text: `is_current` can be `NULL`
choices.why: It is declared `NOT NULL`.

choices.text: A join on a boolean column is not allowed in PostgreSQL
choices.why: It is allowed; it would be wrong.

prompt: Why are facts with no customer given `customer_key = -1` instead of `NULL`?
hint: What does an inner join do with a `NULL` key?

choices.text: `-1` takes less space than `NULL`
choices.why: Space is not the argument.

choices.text: PostgreSQL does not allow `NULL` in a bigint column
choices.why: It does; the column is declared `NOT NULL` on purpose.

choices.text: An inner join keeps the sale
choices.why: Right. With `NULL` it would drop a third of the revenue.

choices.text: `-1` marks the customer for deletion
choices.why: It marks an unknown customer, not a deletion.

prompt: Customer 1880 asked to be erased. What does the warehouse keep of them after the nightly load?
hint: The person goes; the sales stay.

choices.text: Their old versions in `dim_customer`, as history
choices.why: History is not a reason to keep a person the law says to delete.

choices.text: Nothing at all, sales included
choices.why: The sales stay, with no customer.

choices.text: Their sales, under customer key -1
choices.why: Right. Every version is deleted; the sales point at nobody.

choices.text: Their current version only, with the city blanked
choices.why: Every version goes.

prompt: A reader with `lock_timeout = '2s'` queried `marts.dim_shop` during a slow `TRUNCATE` load and failed. Why?
hint: Which lock does TRUNCATE take?

choices.text: The table was empty
choices.why: The reader never got far enough to see it.

choices.text: The strongest lock blocks even readers
choices.why: Right. The reader waited two seconds and gave up.

choices.text: `pg_sleep` blocks every session in the database
choices.why: It only sleeps its own session.

choices.text: Readers need a different role during loads
choices.why: Roles were not involved.

prompt: Match each way of replacing a table's contents to what a reader sees during the load.
hint: Two waits, one sees the old rows, one barely notices.

pairs.left: TRUNCATE and insert, in one transaction
pairs.right: Waits for the whole load, or fails

pairs.left: DELETE and insert, in one transaction
Build a new table, then swap names

prompt: Order the three statements of the type 2 load in `dim_customer.sql`.
hint: Close, open, erase.
items: Close the current version of customers who moved
Open a version for customers with none current
Delete every version of customers the shop no longer has

prompt: A team loads facts by appending each night's new orders, and their scheduler sometimes reruns a night. What is the smallest change that makes reruns harmless?
hint: Make the load know which rows it replaces.

choices.text: Run the scheduler less often
choices.why: A rerun can still happen.

choices.text: Add `SELECT DISTINCT` to every report
choices.why: That hides duplicates in some reports and merges real lines in others.

choices.text: Delete the night's period before inserting it, in one transaction
choices.why: Right. A rerun then replaces the period instead of adding it twice.

choices.text: Switch to a full reload of the whole fact table
choices.why: That also works, at the cost of reloading all history every night.
